name: Nation of Ulysses
label: Dischord
lede: Five DC kids declared themselves a political party, not a band, and wrote a thirteen-point plan to destroy America. Ian Svenonius talked, the trumpet answered, and it lasted four years.

eras.title: A quartet called Ulysses
eras.text: The DC scene had spent the '80s arguing about sincerity. Ulysses showed up in spring 1988 sounding like a revolutionary cell, and when Tim Green joined on second guitar they added the Nation.

years.h: Ulysses: one singer with a trumpet, three bandmates
years.p: [[Ian Svenonius|0ef9be87-0dbe-4551-a526-f3f6891a2e9d]] sings and plays trumpet, Steve Kroner plays guitar, Steve Gamboa bass and [[James Canty|ffc732f4-15a3-42e1-a498-965c1d793e35]] drums. Canty is the younger brother of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] drummer [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]].

years.h: [[Tim Green|19b6bda7-fbb1-4a45-a3c7-687114167e8c]] joins, and Ulysses gets a nation
years.p: Green arrives as second guitarist in late 1989. The band renames itself the Nation of Ulysses to fit its ambitions.

eras.title: The sassiest boy in America
eras.text: The doctrine came before the records. The zine Ulysses Speaks mixed 1960s radicals, French Situationists and juvenile delinquency, and ran nine issues.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Nation of Ulysses · Dischord
years.p: Svenonius writes most of the zine and Green helps with layout. Dischord's bio repeats the zine's own line: a violent separatist political party operating out of Washington.
years.xp: The zine was the manifesto. It blended 1960s-70s radical politics, French Situationist writing and juvenile delinquency into what the band called the Ulysses Aesthetic, and it was handed out at shows and mailed to readers.

years.big: "To create a space of liberation where anything's possible."
years.src: Wikipedia: The Nation of Ulysses · Wikipedia: Ian Svenonius
years.h: Sassy makes Svenonius its first Sassiest Boy in America
years.p: The October 1990 issue of the teen magazine interviews him at length, before the band has a proper record out. He uses the space to call rock a corrupt medium.
years.xp: A glossy magazine for teenage girls met a singer who talked like a pamphlet. In the interview Svenonius described what the band was after and waved off conventional rock groups.

eras.title: Thirteen points, three seven-inches
eras.text: The records came fast, with song titles that read like planks of a party platform. The shows, by Svenonius's own account, cost blood.

years.h: The first seven-inch is Dischord No. 46.5
years.p: Three songs, later tacked onto the CD of 13 Point Program to Destroy America as bonus tracks.

years.src: Dischord · Wikipedia: The Nation of Ulysses
years.h: 13 Point Program to Destroy America, recorded in January
years.p: The debut album was cut at Inner Ear with [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] of [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]] and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]. It runs sixteen tracks, among them Look Out! Soul Is Back and You're My Miss Washington, D.C.
years.xp:
It came out as Dischord No. 57. The liner notes spelled out the dress code: the kids, being utterly disenfranchised, had control over only "clothing and fashion."

Other titles on the record include Hot Chocolate City and A Kid Who Tells On Another Kid is a Dead Kid.
play: A Kid Who Tells On Another Kid is a Dead Kid

years.cap: Ian Svenonius stage-diving at Sacred Heart Church, Washington, DC, 1991
yt: Live at Oz Nightclub, Seattle, 26 Aug 1991
years.h: Svenonius breaks an arm, a leg and his head
years.p: He called Nation of Ulysses shows masochistic, cacophonous and violent, and he remembered the damage by body part.
years.xp: The description comes from Svenonius himself: "an extraordinary freak-out kind of thing," with lots of blood. The fan-archive tapes of Seattle's Oz Nightclub from August 1991 are the closest thing to evidence.

years.h: The Birth of the Ulysses Aesthetic, three songs in a hurry
years.p: Dischord No. 62, again produced by Janney, and subtitled the synthesis of speed and transformation.

eras.title: Memphis, then Nirvana
eras.text: Plays Pretty for Baby went looser and jazzier, and then the ground moved. By fall 1992 the Nation had dissolved.

years.src: Chunklet · Wikipedia: The Nation of Ulysses
yt: Live at the Capitol Theater, Olympia, 1992
years.h: Nobody promoted Memphis, so they flyered it themselves
years.p: Touring with [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]], the band finds its show was never advertised. They paper the streets, run into [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]], and play the Antenna Club to five people, two of them from Primal Scream.
years.xp:
Primal Scream were in town making a record and invited the band into the studio. Nation of Ulysses cut five songs in nine hours on Primal Scream's dime, the Memphis Demos: N-Sub Ulysses, Shakedown and Mockingbird, Yeah among them.

Several of those songs anchor Plays Pretty for Baby.

years.h: Plays Pretty for Baby goes jazz, with MacKaye at the board
years.p: Dischord No. 71, produced by MacKaye at Inner Ear. The titles The Kingdom of Heaven Must Be Taken By Storm and The Sound of Jazz To Come read like slogans.
The guitarist leaves while the band is recording what would have been its third record. Svenonius, Green, Gamboa and Canty carry on as a four-piece.

years.cap: Ian Svenonius in front of a DC flag, club Bratniak, Poznan, circa 1992
years.src: Wikipedia: The Nation of Ulysses · Dischord
years.h: Nirvana arrives, and Nation of Ulysses calls it
years.p: The band breaks up in fall 1992. Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa start the short-lived Cupid Car Club.
years.xp:
Svenonius put it on the calendar: "The epoch changed with the advent of digital music and the Nirvana explosion." What came next, he said, was indie rock, "a sort of vacuous form."

The final sessions, recorded as a four-piece, sat on tape until Dischord put them out as The Embassy Tapes in 2000.

eras.title: The party in exile
eras.text: The Nation never reformed, but nobody stopped working. Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa went straight into the Make-Up, Green into the producer's chair, and the last tapes came out in 2000.

years.cap: Svenonius with the Make-Up at the Empty Bottle, Chicago, October 1998
years.h: The Make-Up takes over from the Nation
years.p: Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa run the new band through 2001. Green becomes an engineer and producer, and plays in [[The Fucking Champs|e786319e-c2df-4409-8e92-55fac38b5841]].
Dischord No. 124 collects the last songs, recorded at The Embassy with MacKaye in September 1992 on half-inch four-track.
years.xp: Kroner had already left, so this is the sound of the unfinished third album as a four-piece.

years.p: Weird War is the first of several Svenonius bands after the Make-Up. Chain and the Gang and Escape-ism come later.

years.h: Svenonius puts the zine's voice in hardcovers
years.p: The Psychic Soviet, his first book of essays, carries the Ulysses Speaks tone into print.

years.cap: Svenonius DJing at the Mercury Lounge, New York, March 2007
years.p: The VBS.tv show runs through 2010 and takes him to places as grand as the Guggenheim.

years.cap: Svenonius with Chain and the Gang, January 2014
years.h: A how-to from the man who tried to end rock and roll
years.p: Supernatural Strategies for Making a Rock 'n' Roll Group is Svenonius's guide to starting a band, written twenty years after he tried to secede from one.
